newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to help cash-hit financial institutions.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to help cash-hit financial institutions.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand said on Tuesday it would help cash-strapped financial institutions by lending funds to them at a lower rate than the prevailing commercial bank minimum lending rate.
The assistance would be given through the central bank's rehabilitation funds with immediate effect, its governor Rerngchai Marakanond told reporters.
"The measure will have immediate effect and aim at helping any financial institution which has liquidity problems," he said.
The loans will be charged at an interest rate of 12.50 percentage points or 50 basis points below the current MLR, he added.
The repayment period of the loans will also be extended to as long as one year from only one month previously implemented, the governor said.

Thailand last month moved to revamp the ailing financial sector by ordering 10 weakened finance companies to boost their capital and directing all financial institutions to raise their provisioning for sub-standard assets.

The move was aimed at boosting public confidence on finance conpanies which have been hit by their large amounts of non-performing loans to the depressed and cash-strapped property sector, analysts said.
Finance companies have also posted weak first quarter results because business and lending has slowed in a sluggish economy.
